# <op> — an operator tree generated by `forge run`

This directory is the **card** of one run: the judge and the clock the student is held to,
the kernel the student starts from, and the records the loop keeps. Nothing in it is written
by hand. It is generated from `tasks/<op>/` by `forge run` (`src/forgekernel/taskcard.py`); to
change anything here, change the task (or `local.env` for the machine) and run `forge run`
again.

## Layout

```
operators/<op>/
  eval/leaderboard/problem.json   the problem: shapes, input groups, the judge's source, the
                                  tolerance frozen by calibration, how the reference is reached
  eval/leaderboard.py             the judge and the clock (copied from the harness; do not edit)
  eval/timing.py, precision.py    timing windows and the precision gate (copied; do not edit)
  eval/closed_ref.py              loads the sealed reference inside a job (copied; do not edit)
  eval/bench.py, eval/ncu_run.py  the bench and the NCU window the jobs run (generated)
  gpu_entry.sh                    the job entry point: correctness | perf | all | ncu | cmd:<...>
  kernel.py | kernel.cu           the student's kernel: the only file the student changes
  window.toml                     the timed-window contract (generated; both sides share one
                                  boundary by construction)
  submit.toml                     where this tree's GPU jobs run (from local.env; rewritten on
                                  every launch)
  submit.local.toml               gitignored: the sealed reference's key (FK_REF_KEY)
  loop.toml                       gitignored: how the loop reads the task (generated)
  ref_bin/                        the sealed reference payload (source mode / blackbox mode)
  milestone.md                    written by the teacher's distillation step, patched in place
  student/status.jsonl            the inner trajectory: one record per student round
  meta_status.jsonl               the outer trajectory: one record per teacher step
  evidence/                       the teacher's pricing ledgers and dossiers (not KB material)
  arch_baseline.json              the reference's measured reading and NCU signature
  best_confirmation.json          the finish: the best kernel re-measured, median against median
```

The student's workspace (`<run>/ws/`) is a single-branch clone of this tree; every student
round is a commit there, pushed back as a branch the GPU job archives (`git archive`). The
`.gitattributes` here lists what never rides into a job (export-ignore); `.gitignore` keeps
the key, the job records and local scratch out of git.

## What the loop holds the kernel to

- **Correctness**: every input group of every shape passes the judge within the tolerance
  frozen at calibration (`problem.json` → `tolerance`).
- **Performance**: the geometric mean over the input groups of a shape, then over the shapes,
  in the task's timing window (`device` by default: pipelined batches ≈ device time; `e2e`
  includes the host tax). The reference, when the task has one, is timed in the same job,
  back to back with the kernel (`eval/timing.py`, mirrored order after a burn-in), so the
  ratio is read on one card in one minute.
- **The evaluator belongs to the card**: `gpu_entry.sh`, `eval/`, `ref_bin/` and
  `.gitattributes` come from here on every job, whatever the student's lineage carries
  (`src/forgekernel/loop/harness_guard.py`); a delivery that edits them is reverted.
- **Host-bound readings are flagged**: `host_enqueue_ms / device_median_ms` close to 1 means
  the device window measured the host's dispatch cost; the reference side is a measurement
  problem, the student side a defect fed back to the student (`src/forgekernel/timing_audit.py`).
- **The correctness monitor** reruns the judge on the confirmed best kernel with new seeds
  and stressed inputs at the finish; it records and never changes a verdict
  ([`docs/correctness-monitor.md`](../../docs/correctness-monitor.md)).
